rules.title: SSL 2.0 / SSL 3.0 Obsolete Protocol Deployment
rules.description: Captured traffic negotiated obsolete SSL 2.0 or SSL 3.0 protocols exhibiting critical cryptanalytic and structural protocol flaws.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed negotiated SSL version 2.0 or 3.0 in handshake server hello.
rules.limitations: Obsolete protocol configuration does not establish active command-and-control communication or adversary-in-the-middle execution.

rules.title: TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1 Deprecated Protocol Deployment
rules.description: Captured traffic negotiated deprecated TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 protocols, which lack modern AEAD ciphers and exhibit downgrade susceptibility.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed negotiated TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 in handshake server hello.
rules.limitations: Passive TLS 1.0/1.1 negotiation does not establish adversary C2 concealment or active interception.

rules.title: Plaintext Transport / NULL Cipher Negotiation
rules.description: Session negotiated unencrypted NULL cipher suite or continued in unencrypted cleartext transport.
rules.evidence_requirements: Cipher suite negotiated with null encryption or cleartext transport observable in session.
rules.limitations: Observable cleartext transport enables passive sniffing without cryptanalysis, but does not identify the capturing adversary.

rules.title: RC4 Stream Cipher Negotiation
rules.description: Session negotiated an obsolete RC4 stream cipher suite with known statistical keystream biases.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed negotiated cipher suite belonging to RC4 family.
rules.limitations: Weak cipher negotiation alone does not confirm adversary C2 tunneling or practical plaintext recovery.

rules.title: 64-bit Block Cipher Deployment (3DES / DES)
rules.description: Session negotiated a 64-bit block cipher susceptible to birthday collision attacks (SWEET32).
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed negotiated cipher suite utilizing 3DES or DES.
rules.limitations: Algorithmic SWEET32 relevance does not confirm birthday collision execution or session cookie extraction.

rules.title: CBC Mode Cipher Suite Usage
rules.description: Session negotiated CBC-mode cipher suite without Encrypt-then-MAC, susceptible to padding oracle attacks.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed CBC-mode cipher suite negotiated in TLS 1.2 or earlier.
rules.limitations: CBC configuration indicates architectural susceptibility; does not confirm chosen-ciphertext padding oracle exploitation.

rules.title: Static RSA Key Exchange (No Forward Secrecy)
rules.description: Session negotiated static RSA key exchange without ephemeral Diffie-Hellman, forfeiting forward secrecy.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed TLS cipher suite utilizing static RSA key exchange without DHE or ECDHE.
rules.limitations: Lack of forward secrecy allows retrospective decryption if server private key is compromised, but does not prove active sniffing or MITM.

rules.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman Modulus (< 2048 bits)
rules.description: Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman exchange utilized a prime modulus smaller than 2048 bits (Logjam susceptibility).
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed ServerKeyExchange DH parameter modulus < 2048 bits.
rules.limitations: Cryptanalytic parameter weakness does not prove discrete logarithm precomputation or active MITM downgrade.

rules.title: Expired X.509 Certificate
rules.description: X.509 certificate validity period expired prior to the session timestamp.
rules.evidence_requirements: Certificate notAfter timestamp strictly precedes session capture timestamp.
rules.limitations: Certificate expiration is a lifecycle management failure; it does not indicate adversary certificate theft or purchase.

rules.title: Premature / Not-Yet-Valid X.509 Certificate
rules.description: X.509 certificate notBefore validity period is in the future relative to the session timestamp.
rules.evidence_requirements: Certificate notBefore timestamp strictly succeeds session capture timestamp.
rules.limitations: Premature validity typically reflects system clock skew or operational misconfiguration, not adversary capability acquisition.

rules.title: Inadequate RSA Public Key Size (< 2048 bits)
rules.description: Certificate public key uses an RSA modulus size below 2048 bits, failing modern security margins.
rules.limitations: Sub-standard key length lowers factorization complexity but does not prove prime factorization execution.

rules.title: Legacy Certificate Signature Algorithm (MD5 / SHA-1)
rules.description: Certificate was signed using MD5 or SHA-1 hash functions that lack collision resistance.
rules.evidence_requirements: Observed signature algorithm using MD5 or SHA-1 digest.
rules.limitations: Weak collision resistance does not confirm that an adversary generated a colliding certificate or impersonated an authority.

rules.title: Self-Signed Certificate Presented in Chain
rules.description: Certificate subject matches issuer with self-verification, lacking verifiable external trust path.
rules.evidence_requirements: Subject matches issuer and certificate verifies with own public key.
rules.limitations: Adversary certificate creation is NOT established. Legitimate internal PKI, local testing, and staging environments are non-adversarial explanations.

rules.title: Explicit STARTTLS Downgrade / Stripping Behavior
rules.description: Observable protocol negotiation indicates cleartext email session failure to execute STARTTLS upgrade.
rules.evidence_requirements: Documented STARTTLS offer stripped or cleartext continuation following failed upgrade.
rules.limitations: Incomplete capture, client configuration, or legitimate operational policies must be ruled out before asserting adversarial manipulation.

rules.title: Server Identity Mismatch (SNI vs SAN)
rules.description: Presented certificate Subject Alternative Name does not match requested Server Name Indication.
rules.evidence_requirements: Conclusive mismatch between SNI and SAN domains with full context.
rules.limitations: Hostname mismatch alone can stem from CDN multi-tenancy or misconfiguration; does not confirm Adversary-in-the-Middle.

rules.title: Certificate Chain Trust Path Validation Failure
rules.description: Presented certificate chain failed validation against trusted authority roots.
rules.evidence_requirements: Conclusive non-empty certificate chain that fails path construction.
rules.limitations: Failed trust-path validation indicates local trust store omission or missing intermediate; does not prove adversarial certificate creation.

rules.title: Cryptographically Verified Revoked Certificate
rules.description: Presented certificate is confirmed revoked via authoritative CRL or verified OCSP response.
rules.evidence_requirements: Authoritative CRL entry or cryptographically verified OCSP response with REVOKED status.
rules.limitations: Revoked certificate indicates cryptographic invalidity; does not infer improper client verification or attacker behavior.
